strengths: Opens on three concrete scenes (door sweets, office boxes, shrinking summer catalogs) before the title question, so the reader knows why the article exists.
The first section answers the search question by splitting omiyage, temiyage, ochugen/oseibo, and okaeshi instead of leaving “gifts” as one mood.
Visitor tips and FAQ give a finishable payoff: what to bring, what not to overspend, how to accept.
The “mild tax” office joke and the trapped-host scenario are the aha moments travelers can use.

issues.location: What Visitors Over-Read + Visitor Tips + FAQ
issues.problem: Modest scale, okaeshi debt, and “not every encounter” are restated three times. A careful reader may skim the last third as a recap.
issues.suggestion: Keep the warning once in Over-Read, once as a short tip; let FAQ stay one-line answers without restating the arms-race metaphor.

issues.location: How Japanese People Experience the Small Bag — internal-link sentence
issues.problem: Bow and “no” links stacked in one sentence read like a sitemap and stall the office-reentry scene.
issues.suggestion: Keep one cross-link; move the other to related reading or a later clause.

issues.problem: Genkan is used without a gloss; first-time readers may miss that the gift is offered at the shoe threshold.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief gloss (entryway where shoes come off) or link the shoes article; do not turn this into a wrapping tutorial.
